After the official shutdown of the TV Time app last month, Antonio Pinto, one of its co-founders, has announced the launch of a brand-new TV and film tracking app called Bingers, with the new version placing greater emphasis on social features. Here are the details.

Bingers is now available for download

Whip Media previously announced the closure of its TV tracking app TV Time, and one of the app's co-founders has immediately announced the launch of Bingers, positioning it as "a fast, beautiful, and fun community-driven watchlist."

Now, according to TechCrunch, Bingers has launched on iOS and Android platforms, providing a spiritual successor for users who have yet to find an alternative—after all, TV Time was once one of the most widely used TV and film tracking apps globally.

Users who previously used TV Time and have saved their data through the platform's export tool before the app's closure can import their archives into Bingers and pick up where they left off; as for users who did not export their data, or those trying a TV tracking app for the first time, they can start from scratch.

Bingers has significantly strengthened its community-driven features, including user profiles, comments, show ratings, GIFs, polls, and character popularity votes. Pinto told TechCrunch that these features were precisely what made TV Time so popular over the years:

For users who simply want to keep track of the TV shows and films they have watched, Bingers offers dedicated watchlist and viewing history features. Similar to TV Time, the app also displays a calendar of upcoming episodes and premiere dates, indicating how many days remain until they officially air.

Bingers is available for free download on the App Store, with no in-app purchases offered at this time.
